entries.title: Add everyone with a reviewer tag to a review plan in one step
entries.summary: The **Add reviewer** dialog on **Reviewers** has a new **By tag** tab: pick one or more reviewer tags (any or all), see who will be added and who is already on the plan, and add them all at once. Nobody is added twice.

where.path: Program → Review → Reviewers (or a plan's Reviewers tab) → Add → Add reviewer → By tag

entries.use_case: When a committee is already tagged by specialty, an admin can put the whole Cardiology panel on a new review plan in one click instead of adding people one at a time, and see exactly who will be added first.

cs_action.note: Nothing to turn on: the By tag tab is in the Add reviewer dialog for every Review Plan 2.0 plan.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reuses the same tagged reviewer groups across plans, or complains about adding reviewers one by one.
internal.who_should_get_it: Sessions 2.0 customers with large review committees who tag reviewers (34 US events tag reviewers today).
internal.staff_path: Program → Review → Reviewers → Add → Add reviewer → By tag
internal.gotchas: Tags must exist and be applied first (Reviewer tags tab). Only people on the Reviewers list match. With no round checked, people join the plan only — check rounds to enroll them. Invites follow the Send invite email switch, like a manual add.
internal.talk_track: If your reviewers are tagged, you can now add a whole tag to a plan at once — you'll see the list and how many are already on it before you confirm.

entries.title: Assign Awards reviewers to a round by tag
entries.summary: A round's **Reviewers** tab has **Assign by tag**: pick program reviewer tags (any or all), preview who joins the round and who is already on it, and add them in one step. Invitations are off by default.

where.path: Awards → (program) → Rounds → (round) → Reviewers → Assign by tag

entries.use_case: When a later round should go to a tagged subset of the panel (say, Senior judges for the final), a program manager can put them all on the round at once instead of editing each reviewer.

cs_action.note: Nothing to turn on: available to program managers on every round.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When an Awards customer runs multi-round judging with different panels per round.
internal.who_should_get_it: Awards customers who use Reviewer Tags (few today — a good reason to introduce tags).
internal.staff_path: Awards → program → Rounds → round → Reviewers → Assign by tag
internal.gotchas: Tags are per program, so only this program's current reviewers match. Logged in the program audit log as Reviewers added by tag.
internal.talk_track: Tag your judges once, then drop a whole tag onto a round — you'll see who's added and who's already there before confirming.

entries.title: Visitors can vote for the posters they rate
entries.summary: Turn on **Attendee voting** on a gallery's **Behavior** tab and every poster carries a vote control, on the card and in the detail view. **Show vote counts** decides whether visitors see the running tally; either way **Most voted posters** ranks them for you on **Analytics**.

enable.path: Publish → Posters → a gallery → Behavior → Attendee voting

where.path: Publish → Posters → a gallery → Behavior

entries.use_case: A poster hall that ran a paper ballot, or no vote at all, can now collect a people's-choice result from the same page visitors are already reading — and see the ranking without counting anything.

cs_action.note: Nothing to turn on beyond the switch on the gallery's Behavior tab; Poster Gallery itself is still per-event Early Access.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any customer running a people's-choice or best-poster award, or asking how to measure which posters landed.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with a Poster Gallery — scientific and medical meetings with a poster hall above all.
internal.staff_path: Publish → Posters → a gallery → Behavior → Attendee voting
internal.gotchas: A public hall has no sign-in: a vote is tied to the visitor's browser, so clearing site data or a private window lets the same person vote again. On a Gated gallery the vote is tied to the verified email. Do not sell it as a ballot — it is a popularity signal, and a customer awarding a prize on it should say so in their own rules.
internal.talk_track: Visitors can now vote on posters straight from the hall, and you get the ranking in Analytics — it is a popularity read, not a secure ballot.

entries.title: Authors can record a poster narration in the browser
entries.summary: The **Narrate your poster** card on an author's session **Files** tab records a walkthrough of up to five minutes — record, play it back, and **Save narration** or **Discard and record again**. Visitors hear it as **Author narration** next to the poster.

where.path: Speaker portal → My Participation → a poster session → Files → Narrate your poster

entries.use_case: An author who could not get an audio file out of their recording software can now narrate their poster from the portal in two minutes, so a visitor reading it months later still hears them explain it.

cs_action.note: Nothing to turn on. The card appears on a session that has a live poster when the event has Poster Gallery.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Customers whose poster halls are read long after the meeting, and anyone who asked for narrated ePosters.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with a Poster Gallery and authors who will not hand over an audio file.
internal.staff_path: View portal as an author → a poster session → Files → Narrate your poster
internal.gotchas: Five minutes and 12 MB. Recording again replaces the previous take — there is no Remove button, though a saved narration can be deleted from the Files list like any other file. The author must allow the microphone; a blocked permission looks like a dead button.
internal.talk_track: Your authors can record a short narration straight from the portal — no software, no file to send you — and visitors hear it beside the poster.

entries.title: Authors can build their poster in the portal
entries.summary: A Poster slot card now offers **Build your poster**: the block editor that organizers use, opened on the author's own session and seeded from the abstract they submitted. **Save draft** keeps the work, **Publish my poster** files it as the session's poster.

where.path: Speaker portal → My Participation → a poster session → Files → Build your poster

entries.use_case: An author with the content but no designed poster can lay one out in the browser from the abstract they already submitted, instead of the organizer building it for them or the session going to the hall empty.

cs_action.note: Nothing to turn on: the link appears on the Poster slot card for events with Poster Gallery.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Customers chasing authors for poster files, or who have been asking staff to build posters from abstracts.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with a Poster Gallery and a long Missing list on Poster coverage.
internal.staff_path: View portal as an author → a poster session → Files → Build your poster
internal.gotchas: A session has one current poster: publishing from the builder replaces an uploaded file as the current one, and an upload afterwards replaces the built one (the earlier file stays in version history). The link only appears in the speaker portal — not on the admin Files list, not in the Public API slot payload.
internal.talk_track: Authors can now build a poster from their abstract in the browser, so a session without a file is not automatically a gap in your hall.

entries.title: Duplicate contacts are suggested from either contact, and any of them can be the primary
entries.summary: Contacts with exactly the same name or email are now always suggested to each other, from either profile. The contact you open is always listed on **Merge Duplicates**, so it can be the primary, and the search box there finds records by email.

where.path: Contact profile → Merge Duplicates

entries.use_case: When the same speaker exists under a work and a personal address, either record now shows the duplicate banner and the admin can keep the one they want as the primary.

cs_action.note: Nothing to turn on; applies wherever duplicate merging is available (Speaker CRM or Unique Contacts).

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that only one of two duplicates shows the banner, or that the record they want to keep is missing from the merge screen.
internal.who_should_get_it: CRM and Unique Contacts customers who merge duplicates, especially after imports from several sources.
internal.staff_path: Contact profile → duplicates banner → Merge Duplicates
internal.gotchas: Fuzzy matches (name variants, similar email prefixes) still come from search and can take a few minutes to appear for a new contact; exact name/email matches appear at once.
internal.talk_track: If two records have the same name or email, you'll see the duplicate from either one now, and you can pick whichever record you want to keep.

entries.title: Filter reviewers and email the ones you pick, with your own message
entries.summary: The **Reviewers** list now filters by plan, reviewer tag and status (**Not emailed yet**, **Emailed**, **No assignments**, **Not started**, **In progress**, **Done**), and **Invert** flips the selection across every matching reviewer. **Email** in the selection bar sends just those reviewers their plan invitation again, or a custom subject, message and button with merge tags such as each reviewer's name, assignment count, deadline and portal link. A per-reviewer preview and **Send a test to me** come before the send.

where.path: Program → Review → Reviewers (or a plan's Reviewers tab) → select reviewers → Email

entries.use_case: Mid-review, an admin can filter to the reviewers who have not started, pick them, and send a personal nudge with their own assignment count and a one-click link to their review portal, instead of emailing the whole plan or relying on the generic invitation.

cs_action.note: Nothing to turn on; it is on every review plan's Reviewers list.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says reviewer emails are too generic, or that the only options are emailing everyone on a plan or resending one invitation at a time.
internal.who_should_get_it: Program customers running large or multi-plan review committees, especially abstract reviews with hundreds of reviewers.
internal.staff_path: Program → Review → Reviewers → filters → select → Email
internal.gotchas: A custom email is tied to one plan per send; the plan invitation can go for every open plan a reviewer is on (one email per plan). Custom copy can go to a closed plan, but the reviewer's portal shows nothing until the plan opens. Reviewers selected but not on the chosen plan are skipped and the dialog says so. Up to 5,000 reviewers per send. Test sends carry [Test] in the subject and go only to the admin. A follow-up web-api change limits custom emails to admins who can update review plans.
internal.talk_track: Filter your reviewers to exactly who you need, say everyone who hasn't started, and send them your own message. Each one sees their own name, how many submissions they have, and a button straight into their review portal.

entries.title: Assignments step: select all shown, invert, and remove reviewers from submissions
entries.summary: Under **Individual reviewers** on a review plan's Assignments step, **Select all *N* shown**, **Invert selection** and **Clear** work on the reviewers the search and tag filter show. **Bulk action: Remove reviewers** takes the ticked reviewers off the chosen submissions in the round, with a **Removal preview** first. Only assignments nobody has started are removed; completed reviews, reviews in progress and declines stay.

where.path: Program → Review → plan → Edit → Assignments → Individual reviewers → Bulk action

entries.use_case: When a reviewer group was assigned to the wrong track, or a reviewer drops out, an admin can pull those reviewers off just the affected submissions in one step without touching any review already started or finished.

cs_action.note: On by default for event review plans.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer needs to undo part of an assignment run, or asks how to take a tagged group off a set of submissions.
internal.who_should_get_it: Program customers who run multi-track or multi-round abstract reviews.
internal.staff_path: Review plan → Edit → Assignments → Individual reviewers → Bulk action: Remove reviewers
internal.gotchas: Remove applies to the round selected at the top and the submissions chosen under Which submissions?. It never removes started, completed or declined reviews, and reviewers stay on the plan; to take people off the plan use Remove from plan on the Reviewers tab. Not offered on Speaker CRM interest-form plans.
internal.talk_track: Pick the reviewers, switch the bulk action to Remove, and Sessionboard shows you exactly which open assignments go before anything changes. Started and finished reviews are never touched.

entries.title: Remove reviewers from a plan in bulk, and duplicate a plan without its reviewers
entries.summary: A plan's **Reviewers** tab can filter by tag or **No assignments in this plan** and **Remove from plan** many reviewers at once, after a preview of who stays. **Duplicate plan** now asks whether to **Copy reviewers and their assignments**, and starts unchecked.

where.path: Program → Review → plan → Reviewers tab; Plan Options → Duplicate plan

entries.use_case: A copied plan no longer drags the whole reviewer roster into every reviewer's portal. Admins can duplicate a plan clean, or trim a copied roster down to the people who actually have work in one action.

cs_action.note: On by default.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When reviewers complain about seeing plans they have nothing to do in, usually after an admin duplicated a plan for another track.
internal.who_should_get_it: Program customers who duplicate review plans per track or per round.
internal.staff_path: Review plan → Reviewers tab → filter → select → Remove from plan
internal.gotchas: Reviewers who saved an answer or declined a submission in the plan stay on it; use Remove on their row to take them off anyway. Unstarted assignments go with removed reviewers. Nothing scored is deleted.
internal.talk_track: Duplicate the plan without reviewers, or clean up a copied roster in one go. Anyone who has already reviewed stays.

entries.title: My Reviews lists only the plans where a reviewer has something to do
entries.summary: The review portal's **My Reviews** no longer lists a plan or round where the reviewer has no assignments once that round has been handed out to other reviewers. Rounds nobody has been assigned in yet still show, as **None assigned**.

where.path: Review portal → My Reviews

entries.use_case: Reviewers on a copied or multi-track plan only see the reviews that are theirs, so they stop asking support why a plan shows nothing to do.

cs_action.note: Automatic.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When reviewers report plans with 0 of 0 or None assigned on My Reviews.
internal.who_should_get_it: Program customers who duplicate review plans or run several tracks with one roster.
internal.staff_path: Preview as reviewer in portal → My Reviews
internal.gotchas: A round where nobody has assignments yet stays visible, so reviewers can see work that is coming. Completed and abstained reviews count as work.
internal.talk_track: Your reviewers now only see the plans where they actually have reviews to do.

entries.title: Abstaining for a conflict records a declared conflict, and the conflict audit handles large plans
entries.summary: When a reviewer abstains with a reason that names a conflict relationship, such as **Author**, **Collaborator** or **Institutional affiliation**, Sessionboard records a declared conflict on that one submission, badges it in the conflict audit and keeps later assignment runs from re-assigning the pair. The conflict audit now lists every conflicting assigned pair in the product on large plans instead of asking you to download it.

where.path: Review plan → Reviewers tab → Conflict audit; review portal → Abstain

entries.use_case: Committees that ask reviewers to pick a conflict type when they abstain get those conflicts on record automatically, so the next round doesn't send the same abstract back to its author, and admins can work the audit on screen even with tens of thousands of assignments.

cs_action.note: Automatic for every review plan with abstaining on.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer's abstention reasons are conflict types and the declared-conflicts card stays empty, or when the conflict audit said there were too many pairs to show.
internal.who_should_get_it: Medical and scientific societies running blind or peer abstract review with conflict-of-interest policies.
internal.staff_path: Review plan → Reviewers tab → Conflict audit / Declared conflicts
internal.gotchas: The declaration covers that one submission only, never the authors' other submissions or their organization. Reasons like Not qualified to review stay plain abstentions.
internal.talk_track: If a reviewer abstains because they're an author or collaborator, that's now recorded as a conflict on that submission, and you can review every conflict in the audit without downloading anything.

entries.title: Recipient merge tags name the additional contact when you send only to additional contacts
entries.summary: With **Send only to additional contacts of recipients**, `{{{recipient.first_name}}}`, `{{{recipient.last_name}}}` and `{{{recipient.email}}}` now fill in with each additional contact's own details instead of the primary contact's. Other recipient field tags are blank in their email.

where.path: Contacts or Sessions → Send → Send Email → Include additional contacts

entries.use_case: An assistant emailed on a speaker's behalf is greeted by their own name, not the speaker's, so emails to coordinators read correctly.

cs_action.note: Automatic.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that emails to assistants greeted them with the speaker's name.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who email speakers' assistants or coordinators through additional contacts.
internal.staff_path: Send Email → Include additional contacts → Send only to additional contacts of recipients → preview
internal.gotchas: Portal login link, sessions summary and module tables still refer to the primary contact, on purpose. Email campaigns' Send individual emails to additional contacts option still renders the primary contact's values.
internal.talk_track: When you email only the assistants, each one now sees their own name in the greeting.

entries.title: Flag over-limit text instead of cutting it off, per form
entries.summary: A new form setting, **Flag over-limit text instead of cutting it off**, lets submitters paste or type past a Text or Text Area question's **Maximum Length**. The full answer is kept, the counter turns red, a message asks them to shorten it, and **Next** and **Submit** stay blocked until it fits. Off by default, on submission forms, follow-up forms, Awards application forms and interest forms.

enable.path: Submission form → Form Settings → Character limits → Flag over-limit text instead of cutting it off

where.path: Submission forms (Form Settings), follow-up forms (Settings step), Awards form builder (Rules tab), interest forms (Details step)

entries.use_case: Submitters who draft abstracts in Word and paste each section no longer lose the end of an answer without noticing. They see exactly how far over they are and trim it themselves, so staff stop emailing people to fix truncated text.

cs_action.note: Off on every form; organizers turn it on per form.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports abstracts or bios arriving cut off, or staff emailing submitters to resend text that was truncated on paste.
internal.who_should_get_it: Medical and scientific societies with strict abstract limits, and any customer whose submitters paste long answers.
internal.staff_path: Form builder → Form Settings → Character limits (CFP); Settings step (follow-up); Rules tab (Awards); Details step (interest forms)
internal.gotchas: Applies to Text and Text Area questions only; Email, URL and Rich Text keep the hard cap. Event application and intake forms don't have the setting. Duplicating a form copies it. The server refuses an over-limit answer whatever the setting, so nothing over the limit is saved.
internal.talk_track: Turn this on and a submitter who pastes too much sees a red counter and a clear message instead of silently losing the end of their abstract.

entries.title: Upload slots: ask only one kind of submission for a file
entries.summary: An upload slot's new **Applies to** setting limits it to **Top-level submissions only**, **Nested submissions only** (for example the posters inside a poster hall block) or **Abstracts only**, or leaves it on **Every submission**. Submission filters narrow it further, and coverage, reminders and the speaker portal all follow it.

where.path: Program Settings → Files → Upload slots → open a slot → Applies to

entries.use_case: An organizer collecting posters only from the posters nested under a poster session, or slides only from accepted abstracts, can say so on the slot, so other submissions are not asked for the file or reminded about it.

cs_action.note: Existing slots stay on Every submission.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer wants a file from subsessions or abstracts only and filters can't express it.
internal.who_should_get_it: Program customers with poster halls, nested sessions or abstract programs using upload slots.
internal.staff_path: Program Settings → Files → Upload slots → slot → Applies to
internal.gotchas: A session the slot stops applying to keeps files already uploaded; they show under Submission files in the portal. Insights slot fields do not apply the scope yet.
internal.talk_track: Tell a slot which kind of submission owes the file, and only those speakers are asked and reminded.

entries.title: Review reminder emails show the event name again
entries.summary: The **Review reminder** email to reviewers filled `{{event.name}}` with nothing on some events, so the subject read *Reminder: your reviews for* with no event. The event name now fills in, including in customized templates.

where.path: Review reminder emails sent to reviewers

entries.use_case: Reviewers who serve on several events see which event's reviews are waiting, right in the subject line.

cs_action.note: Automatic. Some customers got blank-subject reminders between Oct 25 and Nov 2; mention the fix if they ask.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer or reviewer reports reminder emails with a blank event name.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with review reminders on, especially with a customized reminder template.
internal.staff_path: Settings → System emails → Review reminder
internal.gotchas: The same fix fills {{event.name}} in the weekly portal summary and any other system email that had the gap.
internal.talk_track: Review reminders name the event again, so reviewers know which reviews are waiting.

entries.title: The merge screen shows how many sessions each duplicate holds
entries.summary: On **Merge Duplicates**, the **Select Contacts** table has a new **Sessions** column with each record's live session count, so you can see which record holds the person's work before you choose the primary.

where.path: Contact profile → Merge Duplicates → Select Contacts

entries.use_case: When two records for the same speaker exist, the admin can keep the one their sessions already hang off as the primary, instead of guessing from names and emails.

cs_action.note: Automatic wherever duplicate merging is available (Speaker CRM or Unique Contacts).

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks which duplicate to keep as the primary.
internal.who_should_get_it: CRM and Unique Contacts customers who merge duplicates.
internal.staff_path: Contact profile → duplicates banner → Merge Duplicates
internal.gotchas: The count is live sessions only. The same release also stops suggesting pairs a super user marked Not a duplicate on the staff-only review page.
internal.talk_track: Before you merge, you can now see how many sessions each record is on, so you keep the right one.

entries.title: Emailing reviewers skips the ones with nothing assigned in the plan
entries.summary: When you email selected reviewers about one plan, the dialog now says how many of them have no assignments in that plan and skips them by default (**Skip them**). **Email** shows only for admins who can edit review plans, and a custom message or test send needs that permission too.

where.path: Program → Review → Reviewers → select reviewers → Email

entries.use_case: After copying a plan with its whole roster, an admin can email that plan's reviewers without reaching the hundreds who were copied over but have nothing to review.

cs_action.note: Automatic.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer worries a copied plan's roster will get emails about work they don't have.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running several review plans from copies.
internal.staff_path: Program → Review → Reviewers → Plan filter → select → Email
internal.gotchas: The count only appears once one plan is chosen. Clear Skip them to email everyone selected. Team members without permission to edit review plans no longer see Email.
internal.talk_track: Pick the plan and select everyone; Sessionboard leaves out the reviewers who have nothing to do in it unless you tell it not to.

entries.title: Over-limit answers survive a saved draft, and every question shows its limit
entries.summary: On a form with **Flag over-limit text instead of cutting it off** turned on, saving a draft now keeps an over-limit answer as written instead of refusing the save, so nothing is lost while the submitter shortens it; submitting still waits until it fits. Questions with no Maximum Length of their own now show the standard limit (255 characters for Text, 5,000 for Text Area) in the counter, and the setting also applies when an admin adds a submission on someone's behalf.

where.path: Submission, follow-up and org session forms with the setting on

entries.use_case: A submitter who pastes a long abstract section and saves to finish later keeps the full text, and a follow-up form never refuses a submit over a limit it did not show.

cs_action.note: Applies only to forms that have the setting on.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer turns on the over-limit setting, or reports a draft that would not save or a follow-up submit refused with no visible limit.
internal.who_should_get_it: CFP customers whose submitters paste from Word (AUA).
internal.staff_path: Form Settings → Character limits
internal.gotchas: Only on forms with the setting on; off, nothing changes. Long titles keep their full text in the draft and are cut to 255 characters on the session record.
internal.talk_track: With the setting on, nobody loses text: a draft keeps what they pasted, and the form tells them exactly how much to cut before they can submit.

entries.title: A reviewer import with a wrong round name lists the plan's real rounds
entries.summary: When a row in a reviewer or assignment import names a round the plan doesn't have, the error now ends with the plan's round names, for example *Its round is "Abstract Submission Review".*, so the file can be fixed without opening the plan.

where.path: Program → Review → import reviewers or assignments

entries.use_case: A customer who copied a template with "Round 1" into a plan whose round has another name sees the right name in the error and re-uploads once.

cs_action.note: Automatic.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says a reviewer upload failed and they don't know why.
internal.who_should_get_it: Anyone importing reviewers or assignments.
internal.staff_path: History → Imports shows each failed row's message
internal.gotchas: Round names match exactly, ignoring case. Deleted rounds are not offered.
internal.talk_track: If a round name is off, the error tells you what the plan's rounds are actually called.

entries.title: Typed abstain reasons are read more carefully for conflicts
entries.summary: When reviewers type their abstain reason, Sessionboard now reads whole words: reasons such as *Same hospital*, *We co-wrote a paper*, *My mentee* or *I know the PI* become declared conflicts, while *Coincides with my travel*, *Not authorized to view* or *I don't know the topic* stay ordinary abstentions.

where.path: Review plan → round → abstaining with a typed reason

entries.use_case: A committee whose reviewers type their reasons gets the conflicts recorded on the right submissions, without lack-of-expertise abstentions being treated as conflicts.

cs_action.note: Tell customers who use conflict moderation with typed abstain reasons (AUA) that a Dropdown of conflict types on the round is exact; free text is pattern-matched.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer's reviewers abstain with free-text reasons and Declared conflicts looks wrong.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using conflict moderation with free-text abstain reasons (AUA).
internal.staff_path: Review plan → Rounds → Abstaining → reason field type
internal.gotchas: Free text is still pattern-matched; a Dropdown of conflict types is exact. An abstention with no reason still counts as a conflict.
internal.talk_track: Typed reasons now land as conflicts when they describe a relationship, and stay plain abstentions when they're about expertise or time.
